settings.title: Settings

changeHome.moveDesc: Copy this harness's hive (every agent, memory, task) and the semantic-memory palace into the new folder. The old folder is left untouched as a backup you can delete later.

resetConfirm.body: Everything {{godName}} remembers, every agent, the task board and all settings are erased. Running sessions stop, and the app reopens on setup.
resetConfirm.didNotRun: Nothing was erased: the app did not restart. Close Atlas and reopen it, then try again.

general.keepAwakeDesc: Blocks display sleep so schedules and terminals keep firing on time. Costs battery, best on AC.
general.simpleModeDesc: Plain language instead of engineering shorthand, and an app without the terminal, git, model ids or skills. Agents work on their own in this mode, because the questions they would ask are asked in the terminal.
general.desktopNotificationsDesc: Native toasts when an agent finishes or needs your input.
general.autoCompactDesc: Queue /compact for every agent on a schedule (hourly by default; interval in the Triggers tab). Off by default. Long-running agents may overflow their context without it.
general.autoUpdateDesc: Checks every six hours and downloads in the background. Nothing installs until you restart.
general.telemetryDesc: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used). Never prompts, code, paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md.
general.languageDesc: Choose the language for the app interface. English is the default.
general.dangerDesc: Reset wipes {{godName}}'s memories, the entire hive (every agent, message, task, and the board), the semantic-memory palace, and all settings - then takes you back to onboarding.
general.arabicTerminalDesc: Renders terminals with the browser's text engine so Arabic joins and reads right-to-left (xterm has no bidi of its own). Off is the GPU renderer: faster, but RTL-blind. Applies to open terminals and new ones alike.
general.arabicTerminalFollowsLanguage: Following your app language. Switch it here to override that either way. The choice sticks even if you change language again.
general.officeThemeDesc: The colours the office is painted in. "Original" is the art as it ships.

connections.lastRequestUrl: last Request URL - Slack reuses it until you Stop
connections.slackHint: In your Slack app: enable Event Subscriptions, add the message.channels / message.groups bot event, set the Request URL above, and reinstall to your workspace. The tunnel URL changes on every restart, so re-paste it after pressing Start again.
connections.webhooksDesc: One endpoint per caller, each with its own secret and mode. They all share one server, so another webhook costs nothing.

connections.noWebhooks: No webhooks yet. Add one to give a tool a URL it can hand work to.
connections.endpointPlaceholder: starts once the webhook server is listening
connections.webhooksHint: Callers POST to a webhook's URL with its secret in the x-md-webhook-secret header. Each one checks bodies against its own JSON schema. Edit that in the Triggers tab of {{godName}}'s Command Center, where the history of everything that arrived lives too.
connections.orgKeyDesc: How a teammate's install addresses yours.
connections.orgConfigOnly: Configuration only for now. The organisation messaging service does not exist yet, so a key here starts no transport. It is saved, shown in the Triggers tab, and waits.

voice.freeFlowDesc: Push-to-talk dictation: speak, and Groq Whisper drops the text into the queue composer.
voice.groqPlaceholder: gsk_... (get a free key at console.groq.com)
voice.freeFlowHint: Two ways to dictate: click the mic button above Send in the queue composer (click to record, click again to transcribe), or, while viewing any agent's terminal, hold Option (⌥) to talk and release to transcribe. Either way the text lands in the composer draft for you to review before sending. macOS will ask for microphone permission the first time you record.
voice.voiceChatDesc: Talk to the orchestrator in real time. Toggle it on from {{godName}}'s tab; choose which microphone and speaker the voice loop uses here.
voice.openaiKeyDesc1: Talking to {{godName}} runs on OpenAI's Realtime API. Speech in, speech out, over a live connection to {{model}}. That is a different service from the Claude subscription your agents run on, so it needs its own OpenAI API key.
voice.openaiKeyDesc2: Paste it once below. It is encrypted on this machine and never shown again. Each voice session mints its own short-lived token from it, and the key itself never leaves your computer. This is the only place the app asks for it.
voice.keyPlaceholderSaved: key saved: paste a new one to replace it
voice.keySaved: Key saved. Talk is ready. Start it from {{godName}}'s card.
voice.noKey: No key yet. Talk stays disabled until one is saved.
voice.idleDisconnectDesc: How long the voice session stays open with no talking before it auto-closes. It bills per minute while open, so one minute is the sensible default.

triggersTab.intro: The two clocks that act on the floor when you are not at the keyboard: one that hands {{godName}} a recurring prompt, and one that boxes up an agent's context before it fills.
triggersTab.schedulesBlurb: A prompt delivered to an agent on a repeat. Each run is a real turn and costs real tokens, so a schedule earns its place only if you would have asked the same question yourself.
triggersTab.contextBlurb: Summarises an agent's session when it gets too full, between steps rather than mid-task. This is what stops a long-running agent hitting its context limit and losing the thread: leave it on.
triggersTab.webhooksBlurb: Let an outside system post work in.
triggersTab.organisationBlurb: Let a teammate's Atlas message yours.

orgSection.settingsOnly: Settings only, for now. The org messaging service does not exist yet, so a key here starts no connection and nothing is sent or received. It is stored ready for when it does.

contextSection.intro: A rule fires only when both halves agree: the gap since its last run has passed, AND that agent's context is at least as full as the bar. A bar of 0% means the clock alone.
contextSection.compactBlurb: Summarises the context so the thread keeps going.
contextSection.clearBlurb: Discards the context. Nothing is summarised.
contextSection.clearCaution: Clearing throws context away. It is not a smaller version of compaction. An agent mid-task forgets what it was doing. Leave this off unless you keep context another way.
contextSection.extraFocusHint: Appended to the provider's compaction command. Empty sends the bare command.
contextSection.commandHint: Sent literally. Empty sends the bare clear command.
contextSection.contextBarHint: How full the window must be before this may run. 0% = time alone.

workersTab.liveIntro: Short-lived agents {{godName}} starts for a single job. workersTab.preservedIntro: Finished workers whose worktree held un-integrated work. Kept (never auto-discarded) and auto-reclaimed once the work lands in its base branch.

quitWarning.bodyComplete: Every agent saved its memory and the orchestrator confirmed the shutdown. The harness closes itself in a moment.
quitWarning.bodyRunning: The orchestrator broadcast closing time. Every worker parks its work, saves its memory, and reports back. The app closes only after the orchestrator confirms nothing will be lost.
quitWarning.ackNoWorkers: No workers on the floor. Waiting for the orchestrator.
quitWarning.timeoutNote: This is taking a while. An agent may be mid-compaction or deep in a tool call. Keep waiting, or force quit and accept the data loss.
quitWarning.runningBody_one: Closing the harness will terminate the running session and discard any unsaved progress it was holding in memory. The conversation history inside it is lost when the PTY exits.
quitWarning.runningBody_other: Closing the harness will terminate all {{count}} running sessions and discard any unsaved progress they were holding in memory. The conversation history inside each session is lost when the PTY exits.
quitWarning.tip: Tip: closing time is the safe way out. The orchestrator has every agent commit its work and save its memory, and the app closes itself once the whole floor has confirmed. No data loss.

hivePicker.title: Choose a workspace
hivePicker.blurb: A workspace is one folder holding one crew: its agents, their memory, the task board and the history. They are separate, so you can keep work apart and switch between them.
hivePicker.deleteBody: This removes the crew in {{name}}: every agent, their memory and sessions, the task board and the history. Your own files in that folder stay. It cannot be undone.
hivePicker.resetTitle: Delete this workspace and reset Atlas?
hivePicker.resetBody: This workspace is open, so deleting it resets the app: the crew in {{name}} is erased and Atlas restarts at setup. Your own files in that folder stay. It cannot be undone.
hivePicker.deleteOpen: Delete this workspace and reset Atlas
hivePicker.newHint: Created under ~/Atlas if it does not exist. Its crew, memory and board live here.

updateBadge.manualBody: Download the latest version and replace the app you have. Prefer the app to update itself? Settings → Updates.
updateBadge.afterBody: When it lands, quit this app and install the new version over the current one. Open it and
updateBadge.upToDate: You are on the latest version.

updateToast.restartWhenever: Restart Atlas whenever you like to apply it. Nothing restarts on its own.
updateToast.manualOnly: This install cannot update itself. Grab the new build from the releases page.
updateToast.agentsWorking: {{names}} are mid-task. Restarting kills the turn they are in — restart from Settings → Updates when the floor is quiet.
updateToast.confirmBodyWorking: {{names}} are working right now. Restarting quits Atlas and kills every agent process: notes, tasks and messages on disk survive, and the crew comes back on the new version resuming their own threads — but whatever they are part-way through is lost.
updateToast.confirmBodyIdle: Atlas quits and reopens on the new version. Your agents are respawned afterwards and resume their own threads; nothing on disk is affected.
